title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: MCP-based agents for US Government clouds
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap launch while preserving Microsoft's conflicting government-cloud availability guidance. The blocking control, general agent entitlements and newly described GCC tool-access control are supported; the government-specific gaps remain appropriately qualified.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: An MCP plugin is a custom action within a declarative agent.
claims.quote: MCP and API plugins are custom actions that enable declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot to interact with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers

claims.claim: The plugin manifest connects the declarative agent to a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server

claims.claim: The plugin manifest does not package or host the running MCP server.
claims.quote: it doesn't package or host the running server.

claims.claim: Copilot resolves a declarative-agent MCP plugin's tools dynamically from the MCP server at runtime by default.
claims.quote: For plugins based on an MCP server, Copilot resolves the plugin's tools dynamically at runtime by default, directly from the MCP server.

claims.claim: A developer can instead pin a fixed tool set in the plugin manifest.
claims.quote: When building the agent, a developer can optionally pin a fixed set of tools in the plugin manifest instead.

claims.claim: Learn does not specifically describe this roadmap item's government MCP enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: "MCP" "Government" "564607" default rollout licensing. Opened build-mcp-plugins, overview-plugins, known-issues, overview-declarative-agent and Copilot service description; found general and conflicting cloud guidance, not documentation specific to this item.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An MCP plugin sends requests to a separately hosted server outside Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The agent sends a request to the plugin's MCP server or API, which is hosted outside of Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: MCP calls are subject to the server's authentication requirements.
claims.quote: If the plugin's MCP server or API requires authentication, the plugin requests a token or API key from the token store.

claims.claim: The agent's access through its plugin remains subject to permissions.
claims.quote: A plugin doesn't grant a user access to data that the user or component isn't otherwise authorized to access.

claims.claim: An agent's available MCP tools depend on its tool configuration.
claims.quote: For a plugin with a pinned tool set, or for a REST API plugin, the agent uses the tools defined in the plugin manifest instead.

claims.claim: Learn does not specify how these separately hosted MCP servers relate to the government-cloud boundary.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP server government cloud data boundary GCC. Opened overview-plugins, build-mcp-plugins and data-privacy-security; read gov-overview search excerpts. General Copilot residency statements do not specify remote MCP-server placement for this item.

claims.claim: Learn states that agents grounded in shared tenant work data are not currently available in GCC, GCCH or DoD.
claims.quote: Agents grounded in shared tenant work data aren't currently available in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud High (GCCH), or Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: The MCP walkthrough uses an OAuth client to obtain an access token on behalf of the signed-in user for each MCP-server call.
claims.quote: Copilot then uses the registration to obtain an access token on behalf of the signed-in user each time the agent calls the MCP server.

claims.claim: Learn allows authentication type None for an MCP server still in development.
claims.quote: If your MCP server is still in development and doesn't implement authentication, select None as the authentication type.

claims.claim: Learn says to add authentication before deploying that server to production.
claims.quote: Add authentication before you deploy to production.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MCP and API custom actions can, when supported, create, update and delete connected-system data through natural-language prompts.
claims.quote: users can ask a declarative agent to query an MCP server or REST API for information and, when supported, create, update, and delete data and objects through natural language prompts.

claims.claim: Dynamic discovery permits the available tool set to change without repackaging and republishing the agent.
claims.quote: Dynamic tool discovery means you get the latest tools the MCP server exposes without waiting for the agent to be repackaged and republished.

claims.claim: Agents published by the organisation go through admin approval before organisation members receive them.
claims.quote: Before you make these agents available to members of your organization, these agents go through an admin approval to ensure compliance and readiness.

claims.claim: Administrators can review the agent list at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide agent-block path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent > Save.
claims.quote:
In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.
In the Block agent or Unblock agent pane that opens, select either Block agent or Unblock agent, and then select Save.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks the selected Copilot package to prevent its use.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The general block control applies to the selected agent and restricts its use across the organisation.
claims.quote:
These actions apply to the selected agent.
Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: Blocking the selected agent does not necessarily block a shared MCP server.
claims.quote: If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections.

claims.claim: Agent blocking does not necessarily revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.
claims.quote: Agent approval or blocking doesn't necessarily grant or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.

claims.claim: The block API is a preview operation under Microsoft Graph beta.
claims.quote: | Block (preview) | POST /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block | Block a package to prevent its usage. |
